subject: East and Central Africa sent 80,763 international passengers into Nairobi's JKIA in September, more than Europe's 61,893, and every route announced this week adds to that side of the ledger
preview: KNBS's September indicators put East and Central Africa first among JKIA's arrival regions at 80,763, ahead of Europe at 61,893 and the Middle East at 54,246 (KNBS Leading Economic Indicators, via Kenyans.co.ke, 18 Nov).

big_reads.title: Uganda's shilling fell 16 per cent this year. Rwanda's franc fell 2. The same dollar rate card now means four different things.
Tanzania doubled the beds inside its national parks. The 160 sites it has just put on the market are in the parks nobody flies to.
Kenya is first on the list for a levy on business class arrivals. The row of numbers behind it does not add up.
Uganda has cut the gorilla permit price in April, May and November. May was its busiest month of the year.
India got a daily flight to Tanzania this morning. The guest on it is worth $276 a night less.
Uganda counted 1.6 million visitors last year. Its holiday arrivals grew by 0.4 per cent.
